sources.title: Calvin Lunsford Beale
sources.locator: Biographical paragraphs describing his Washington education and federal career
sources.rights_notes: Institutional memorial. The project retains only a short excerpt and paraphrase. Its sequence places the Veterans Administration before the OSS but does not explicitly say that the transfer was immediate.

sources.title: Calvin L. Beale, 85; expert on nation's rural population
sources.locator: Biographical section describing Wilson Teachers College and wartime work in the OSS map department
sources.rights_notes: Reputable obituary used for identity corroboration and OSS role context. No postwar career claim is imported into the pre-OSS affiliation dataset.

sources.title: Obituaries: Calvin L. Beale, 85, Demographer
sources.locator: Career chronology noting Veterans Administration and OSS work during World War II and Census Bureau work from 1946
sources.rights_notes: Reputable obituary. Because it shares an author with the Los Angeles Times version, the two are not counted as independent evidence.

organizations.normalization_notes: The AAG memorial prints Veteran's Administration. The historically established agency name is retained canonically; no modern successor name is substituted for the 1942 affiliation.

affiliations.date_precision: The AAG memorial says Beale's federal career began at the Veterans Administration in 1942 and included OSS and Census jobs; it does not state his VA end date or explicitly describe a direct transfer.
affiliations.research_notes: The source's career sequence makes VA the best-supported predecessor found, but no direct before-joining, recruited-from, or transfer wording establishes immediacy. It is published as a qualified earlier government assignment and excluded from default high-confidence employer analytics.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Calvin L. Beale is a high-confidence match to Washington demographer Calvin Lunsford Beale, who held a wartime job in the OSS map department.
claims.evidence_excerpt: found a job in the map department of the Office of Strategic Services
claims.evidence_paraphrase: An institutional memorial and a reputable obituary identify Calvin Lunsford Beale as a Washington federal employee who worked for OSS during World War II.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence. The exact uncommon full name and middle initial, Washington base, civilian federal career, explicit OSS employment, and compatible wartime age provide multiple corroborating identifiers; the index supplies no unique service number.
claims.temporal_assessment: Beale's federal career began in 1942, his OSS work occurred during World War II, and he joined the Census Bureau in 1946. The exact OSS entry and exit dates remain unknown.
claims.match_notes: The AAG memorial is independent of Matt Schudel's two newspaper versions. The profile remains high confidence rather than confirmed until Box 43 supplies a direct identifier.

sources.excerpt_override: included jobs in the Office of Strategic Services

claims.claim_text: Calvin L. Beale began his federal career at the Veterans Administration in 1942 before later wartime OSS work, but the source does not prove that VA immediately preceded OSS.
claims.evidence_excerpt: career in the federal government began at the Veteran's Administration in 1942
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The AAG memorial starts Beale's federal chronology at the Veterans Administration in 1942 and then lists OSS and Census employment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The indexed identity is high confidence from the exact name, explicit OSS role, Washington setting, federal employment, and compatible age and civilian grade.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sequence supports VA as a probable predecessor, but the source supplies no VA end date or explicit direct-transfer language; immediacy remains unresolved.
claims.match_notes: Published as a qualified government assignment, not a settled immediate affiliation or private employer. Box 43 is required to resolve the transition.

research_attempts.query_text: William J Beach OSS; Office of Strategic Services; 2nd Lt; private officer identifier; NARA OSS/index context; official Army bulk file; CIA Reading Room; Library of Congress; employer 1940; occupation; obituary; directory; newspaper; institutional and archival searches
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Five exact-name enlisted records had different private identifiers; the official bulk file does not cover officer numbers. An Army Aviation postwar Captain and other directory, cemetery, genealogy, and Veterans History Project namesakes lacked the indexed identifier and OSS linkage.
research_attempts.research_notes: The staged official, CIA, LoC, exact-name OSS, employment, occupation, obituary, directory, newspaper, institutional, and archival protocol was completed without the authenticated NARA API. No candidate met the common-name identity rule.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 43 and Army officer records.

research_attempts.query_text: Calvin L Beale OSS; Calvin Lunsford Beale Office of Strategic Services; CAF-4; Veterans Administration; map department; NARA OSS/index context; CIA Reading Room; Library of Congress; employer 1940; occupation; obituary; university; institutional and archival searches
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: A 1944 Evening Star hit concerned a relative's obituary, not Calvin's employment; derivative summaries and postwar-only career sources were excluded from the pre-OSS claim. The two Matt Schudel obituary versions were not counted as independent evidence.
research_attempts.research_notes: AAG and a reputable obituary establish a high-confidence exact identity and OSS map-department role. AAG starts the federal career at VA in 1942, but no source explicitly establishes the VA-to-OSS transition, so the affiliation remains medium and qualified.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 43 and VA personnel records to confirm identity and chronology.
